definitions.explanation: A period of three years, or the third year in a sequence.

examples.japanese: {三年|さんねん}{前|まえ}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した。
{日本|にほん}に{来|き}てから{三年|さんねん}になる。
examples.english: It's been three years since I came to Japan.

examples.japanese: この{計画|けいかく}は{完成|かんせい}まで{三年|さんねん}かかった。
examples.english: This project took three years to complete.

notes:
{三年|さんねん} can mean either 'three years' (duration) or 'third year' (position in a sequence, e.g., school year).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {三年|さんねん}{前|まえ} (three years ago)
- {三年|さんねん}{後|ご} (three years later)
- {三年|さんねん}{間|かん} (for three years — with {間|かん} to emphasize duration)
- {三年|さんねん}{目|め} (the third year — ordinal)
- {三年生|さんねんせい} (third-year student)

YEAR COUNTING:
Years use {年|ねん}: {一年|いちねん}, {二年|にねん}, {三年|さんねん}, {四年|よねん} (note: {四|よ}, not し).

CULTURAL NOTE:
{石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん} is a proverb meaning 'perseverance prevails' (literally 'three years on a stone'). Three years is a culturally significant timeframe in Japan — often the expected period to give something a fair try.
